newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium troops ready to evacuate citizens from Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Belgium troops ready to evacuate citizens from Zaire.

text.p: Belgium plans to send troops to states bordering Zaire for a possible evacuation of Belgians from its troubled former colony, a government official said on Saturday.
The troops will probably be sent to Brazzaville, the capital of Congo, which lies just across the Zaire river from the Zairean capital Kinshasa, he said.
BRTN television said 20 paratroopers would initially be sent to Brazzaville, while 15 would be sent to guard the Belgian embassy in Kinshasa. The main force, 550 soldiers, would be sent on Monday.
France and the U.S. have also announced preparations for possible evacuation missions.
"We want to have a unit in place soon for a reconnaissance mission," the official said, adding that Belgium urged all its citizens to leave Zaire as soon as possible.
Earlier on Saturday, some 60 Belgians arrived in Brussels airport on a Sabena flight from Kinshasa.

"It is best to leave now with regular flights, an evacuation will proceed in much more difficult circumstances, especially for children," an official from Belgium's embassy in Kinshasa told VTM television.
A Belgian nun who fled the interior warned against Zairean army soldiers fleeing from Kabila's forces.
"The Zairean army is moving backwards. They are losing, and therefore they are plundering," she said.
Belgian media have estimated the number of Westerners in the Zairean capital at about 7,000, including fewer than 3,000 Belgians, about 1,000 French and 650 Americans.

On Thursday, France sent extra troops to states neighbouring Zaire, including 90 to Brazzaville, in preparation for a possible evacuation. The U.S. is sending hundreds of troops to several West African countries, the Pentagon said on Friday.

Zaire is in deep crisis. Long-time ruler President Mobutu Sese Seko, 66, is gravely ill with cancer and rebels led by Laurent Kabila have seized about a fifth of the sprawling central African country.

Since giving independence to its Congo colony in 1960, Belgium has sent troops back during many crises, most recently in 1993, when 650 paratroopers evacuated nationals from a Kinshasa overrun by rioting Zairean soldiers.
While Belgium cut diplomatic ties with Mobutu in 1990, economic ties with the former colony remain strong, with many Belgian companies active in banking, mining, textiles, brewing and cattle raising.
Kabila, in an interview with Belgian television RTBF from eastern Zaire broadcast on Saturday, said that Belgium had made no contact with him.

"The Belgians never came here. Even the French, who support (Mobutu's) regime with arms have had the guts to send their representatives, but the Belgians, never. They want Mobutu to be the King of Congo," he said.
